paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
model_annotation: The bar charts illustrate the relationship between inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss Kappa, and two different metrics of ambiguity: standard deviation of ambiguity (left chart) and maximum ambiguity (right chart). The vertical axis for both charts is labeled "Fleiss Kappa," displaying a scale from 0.0 to 1.0. The values on this axis range from 0.0 to 0.89, indicating varying levels of agreement among annotators. In the left chart, the ambiguity standard deviation is categorized on the horizontal axis with four bins labeled 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, with corresponding Fleiss Kappa values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24, represented by bars in varying shades of blue. The tallest bar at 0.88 corresponds to the lowest ambiguity (0.0), while the shortest at 0.03 corresponds to an ambiguity standard deviation of 0.82. The right chart categorizes maximum ambiguity values on its horizontal axis, labeled with three categories: 1, 2, and 3, having Fleiss Kappa values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23 respectively. The tallest bar at 0.89 correlates with the highest maximum ambiguity of 1, while the bar for maximum ambiguity of 3, at 0.23, is the shortest. Both charts are sorted in descending order based on the heights of the bars. Each bar is individually labeled with its corresponding Fleiss Kappa value at the top for clarity.
